questions.text: Are you working or studying at the moment?
questions.say: Good afternoon. My name is Emma, and I'm your examiner today. This is the Speaking test. In this first part, I'd like to ask you some questions about yourself. Let's talk about what you do. Are you working or studying at the moment?

questions.text: Do you use English in your work or studies?
questions.say: Do you use English in your work or studies?

questions.text: Do you have enough free time with your work or studies?

questions.text: How many hours a day do you usually spend working or studying?
questions.say: How many hours a day do you usually spend working or studying?

cueCard.topic: Describe something expensive that you would like to own.
cueCard.explain: and explain why you would like to own it.

questions.text: Describe something expensive that you would like to own.
questions.say: Thank you. Now, in Part 2, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. Describe something expensive that you would like to own. You should say: what it is; how much it costs; where you could buy it; and explain why you would like to own it.

questions.text: Do you think you will buy it one day?
questions.say: Thank you. Do you think you will buy it one day?

questions.text: Why do some people buy expensive brands?
questions.say: Thank you. We've been talking about something expensive that you would like to own, and I'd like to discuss with you some more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all expensive things. Why do some people buy expensive brands?

questions.text: Are expensive products always better than cheap ones?
questions.say: Are expensive products always better than cheap ones?

questions.text: Do people in your country show their wealth by what they buy?
questions.say: Do people in your country show their wealth by what they buy?

questions.text: Do people today buy more than they really need?
questions.say: Now let's talk about luxury and consumerism. Do people today buy more than they really need?

questions.text: How does advertising encourage people to buy things they don't need?
questions.say: How does advertising encourage people to buy things they don't need?

questions.text: Will people buy fewer things in the future to protect the environment?
questions.say: Will people buy fewer things in the future to protect the environment?
